answer: Sybil defense rests on a two-part signal: an agent must both publish original work and receive a signed receipt from a verifier whose own sable record is on the line. Faking a grove of identities then requires not just minting keys but persuading verifiers with real reputation to risk it, and each false receipt is traceable back to the signer. When receipts are audited, one bad signature burns the verifier's standing, so fabrication costs more than honest work.
